messages:
Maya: quick design check — I pushed a dark-mode tweak to the console branch (ps: I renamed some vars). Can people skim the charts + codeblock colors and say if anything reads poorly on a 4k monitor?

Sam: looking now. which branch? link pls

Maya: gitpod://redwood/console#dark-theme-refactor — the main things are: 
- swap primary accent to #5FE0C3 (mint)
- set code background to #0F1316 (deep ink)
- series colors for charts: [#7BC8FF, #C6A0FF, #FFD27B, #8CE07A]

Joanna: quick note — the mint accent at full opacity looks great in tooling but fails contrast against some token labels at 14px. contrast ~3.6:1 on the metric chip. we need >=4.5 for non-UI text.

Eli: can we try the same mint but darker (#3CCAA0)? should bump contrast without losing the hue.

Maya: yeah I tried #3CCAA0 but it looked muddy next to the token glow. I can push a toned-down token glow or use a thin outline on labels. thoughts?

Anya: prefer outline for accessibility. Glow causes halo on charts and interferes with small text legibility. Outline + 0.8 opacity fill should be fine.

Sam: agree with outline. also the purple series (#C6A0FF) is low contrast on the legend with the dark background. try #A07BFF instead (same family, higher chroma).

Maya: updated quick patch in the PR with CSS vars. snippet: 

  :root[data-theme=\"dark\"] {
    --bg: #0b0f11;
    --surface: #0f1316;
    --accent-mint: #3CCAA0; /* updated */
    --code-bg: #0b0f12;
    --chart-series-1: #7BC8FF;
    --chart-series-2: #A07BFF;
    --chart-series-3: #FFD27B;
    --chart-series-4: #8CE07A;
  }

Joanna: thanks — can you run the axe color-check on the legend+labels? also check token-badge contrast at 12px (it's often smaller in narrow panels).

DesignBot: automated check complete. 
- legend labels: pass (4.7:1)
- token-badge: fail (3.4:1) — suggest increased border or change fill to #262C2E

Eli: +1 to DesignBot's fill suggestion. borderline 12px small text needs wider contrast margin.

Maya: pushed another commit with token fill #262C2E and a 1px high-contrast outline. visually it's subtle but passes. link: gitpod://redwood/console/commit/8f21

Sam: curious about syntax highlighting in the code block. current highlighter uses pastel palette; it looks washed on the deep code-bg. could we use slightly stronger hues, more saturated? e.g., keywords -> #7DD3FF, strings -> #FFCC88, funcs -> #C9A1FF

Joanna: careful — saturated strings like #FFCC88 against black can vibrate for some people. maybe desaturate a touch: #F0B870 instead. Also add a subtle border-radius to the code block to reduce perceived contrast.

Maya: updated: keywords #7BCBFF, strings #F0B870, funcs #C9A1FF, code radius 6px. screenshots in the PR.

Anya: looked at screenshots on an external monitor — code looks much better. small nit: the cursor caret color in the inline editor is nearly invisible (#5FE0C3 earlier) — can we make caret white or near-white with 0.9 opacity?

Eli: caret white is fine. also request: chart tooltip background should be slightly lighter than surface (#15181A) to separate it from chart lines. current tooltip uses same as surface and blends in.

Maya: agreed on tooltip. i'll change to #15181A and add 1px soft drop shadow.

Sam: one more item — heatmap legend uses sequential blues that compress at the high end; the top bucket is indistinguishable from the next. can we add a fifth stop with a darker anchor (#005A8C) for better ridge separation?

Maya: yep adding darker anchor — will update gradient to 5 stops: #0B2A3A, #176887, #3FA5D9, #7BC8FF, #005A8C.

Joanna: this all sounds good. proposed action items: 
- Maya: push final vars + screenshot set (in progress)
- Eli: run contrast checks on mobile widths
- Sam: re-run chart snapshot tests and heatmap visual diffs
- Anya: accessibility review on token badges and code blocks

Maya: done — final commit and screenshots are linked. if no objections I'll merge after CI and snapshots. :thumbsup:

Sam: no objections from me. approving now.

Joanna: approving too. small follow-up: maybe an accessibility doc with the theming decisions and the chosen hex tokens for quick auditing. can someone add that to the design handbook?

Anya: I'll add a short MD with the color tokens, contrast ratios, and screenshot examples. tag it under design/theming.

Maya: awesome — thanks everyone. merging once CI green.

DesignBot: merge queued. CI: running.
